overview.reclaim: About {size} could go without touching anything you made.

scan.hint: Scan this drive to see what is filling it, folder by folder.
scan.stopped: The scan stopped before it finished.

map.empty: Nothing in here takes up any room.
map.missing: This folder is not in the last scan. Scan again to see it.
map.not_allowed_long: You are not allowed to look inside this folder.
map.rest_sub: Too small to list one by one

trash.confirm_body: “{name}” ({size}) goes to the trash. The space comes back once the trash is emptied.
trash.failed: “{name}” could not be moved to the trash.

clean.intro: About {size} could go without touching anything you made. Each item asks before it deletes.
clean.measuring: Measuring caches, old packages and the trash…
clean.no_pkexec: pkexec is not installed, so nothing here can run as root.
clean.nothing: Nothing here is worth clearing right now.

cache.confirm_body: Nothing you made is kept in here.

trash.body: {n} items you deleted, still taking up room.
trash.confirm_body: Everything in it is deleted for good. This cannot be undone.
trash.title: Trash

pacman.body: pacman keeps every package it downloads: {old} older versions of what you have, and {gone} belonging to software you removed. The version you have installed stays.
pacman.confirm_body: pacman -Sc runs as root and keeps only the packages you have installed. Downgrading to an older version would mean downloading it again.
pacman.title: Old package downloads

orphans.body: {n} packages were installed for something that is gone: {names}.
orphans.confirm_body: pacman -Rns removes them. Each was pulled in by something no longer installed. If you use one of them directly, install it on purpose first.
orphans.title: Unused dependencies

journal.body: The journal takes {total}. Shrinking it keeps the newest {keep}.
journal.confirm_body: journalctl deletes the oldest log files until {keep} is left.
journal.title: System logs

coredumps.body: {n} memory snapshots saved when programs crashed. They only matter if you are debugging those crashes.
coredumps.confirm_body: The saved crash dumps are deleted for good.
coredumps.title: Crash dumps

flatpak.body: {n} runtimes that no installed app needs any more.
flatpak.confirm_body: flatpak uninstall --unused removes them. Apps that need one later download it again.
flatpak.title: Unused Flatpak runtimes

othercaches.body: Kept by your apps, biggest first: {list}. Close an app before clearing its cache by hand.
othercaches.title: Other app caches

downloads.body: {n} items in Downloads have not changed in {days} days.
downloads.title: Old downloads

thumbnails.title: Thumbnails
thumbnails.body: Small previews of your pictures and videos, made again as folders are opened.

pip.title: pip downloads
pip.body: Python packages pip downloaded, fetched again when a project needs them.

yay.title: yay build files
yay.body: Sources and builds left over from installing AUR packages.

paru.title: paru build files
paru.body: Sources and builds left over from installing AUR packages.

npm.title: npm cache
npm.body: JavaScript packages npm downloaded, fetched again when a project needs them.

yarn.title: Yarn cache
yarn.body: JavaScript packages Yarn downloaded, fetched again when a project needs them.

bun.title: Bun cache
bun.body: JavaScript packages Bun downloaded, fetched again when a project needs them.

gobuild.title: Go build cache
gobuild.body: Compiled Go packages, rebuilt on the next build.

nodegyp.title: node-gyp headers
nodegyp.body: Headers for building native Node modules, downloaded again when needed.

cargo.title: Cargo registry
cargo.body: Crates Cargo downloaded, fetched again on the next build.

gradle.title: Gradle caches
gradle.body: Dependencies of Java and Android builds, fetched again on the next build.

maven.title: Maven repository
maven.body: Dependencies of Java builds, fetched again on the next build.

electron.title: Electron downloads
electron.body: Electron builds that development tools downloaded.

shaders.title: Shader caches
shaders.body: Compiled shaders. Games and apps build them again, so their next start is slower.

shadersdb.title: Shader caches
shadersdb.body: Compiled shaders. Games and apps build them again, so their next start is slower.

large.need_scan: Scan a drive on the Overview tab to list its biggest files here.
large.sub: Your biggest files on the scanned drives. Not deleted from here unless you say so.

dupes.group: {n} copies of {name}. Keeping one gets {size} back.
dupes.sub: The same file in more than one place, matched by size and by samples of what is inside. Keeping one of each gets {size} back.

drives.eject_body: Every mounted partition on it is unmounted, then the drive is powered off. Anything using it (a media server, open files) loses it until it is plugged in again.
drives.settings_body: Low-space warnings and emptying old trash are plugin settings.
drives.trim_body: Tells each SSD which blocks are free, which keeps writes fast. This is fstrim.timer, and changing it asks for your password.

health.failing: The drive reports it is failing. Back up what matters on it.
health.unchecked: Health not checked. Reading it needs your password.

low_space_warning.label: Warn when space runs low
low_space_warning.description: Notify when the system filesystem, or the one your home folder is on, drops below the threshold. Checked every ten minutes.

low_space_percent.label: Warn below (% free)
low_space_percent.description: Free space, in percent of the filesystem, that triggers the warning.

empty_trash_after.label: Empty old trash automatically
empty_trash_after.description: Permanently delete items that have been in the trash longer than this. Checked at startup and every six hours.

show_free.label: Show free space
show_free.description: Show the free space next to the glyph instead of the glyph alone.

mount.label: Filesystem
mount.description: Mount point whose free space the bar shows, for example / or /home.
